assessment: The randomized crossover found an inconclusive constipation subscore change with freeze-dried blueberry powder in functional gastrointestinal disorders. The preparation and population differ from raw blueberries in Parkinson disease.
The intervention was bottled green tea. Caffeine is a tea constituent and no arm consumed brewed coffee.
The acute green tea comparison measured drowsiness and local discomfort in healthy men using a fixed session order. It supplies no Parkinson fatigue severity estimate.
Participants were asked to avoid coffee. Both randomized groups received powdered green tea and there is no coffee arm.
The healthy volunteer trial compares two powders and lists a fatigue VAS in Methods without a fatigue result in the human outcome tables.
Participants avoided caffeine before testing. The intervention was date flesh, and the discussion cites a separate soluble coffee trial in healthy older adults.
Sage is the publisher credited for a diagram. No crossover condition used culinary sage.
Green beans refers to unroasted coffee beans in the design justification. The trial gives no culinary green bean comparison.

Chicken was one sandwich filling offered at the start of a study session. The randomized treatments were coffee and chlorogenic acid preparations or placebo. The paper gives no fatigue comparison by sandwich filling.
The decaffeinated soluble coffee and isolated chlorogenic acid comparison gave no clear treatment effect on the mental-fatigue item in healthy older adults.
